arms.predicted: Simulated annealing over item orderings combined with a residual gap-filling pass will achieve a score above 95.0, improving over iter-1's 94.84 hill-climbing approach.
arms.observed: Score: 95.21 (deterministic across 3 runs). The key improvement came from SA over a JOINT space of item orderings + per-item heuristic assignments, not from gap filling. The original SA-only-over-orderings (with fixed heuristic per run) scored 94.84 — identical to iter-1's hill-climbing. Adding per-item heuristic selection to the SA search space unlocked the 0.37-point improvement. Gap filling contributed 0.0 points.
arms.diagnostic_note: The predicted mechanism (SA escaping local optima in ordering space) was partially wrong. For M=8-12, hill-climbing already finds near-optimal orderings. The actual gain came from expanding the search space to include per-item heuristic assignments — a dimension hill-climbing didn't explore. Two initial SA attempts over orderings-only matched hill-climbing exactly (94.84), confirming the ordering space was already well-explored.

arms.predicted: SA without gap filling will score above 95.0 but below h-main, demonstrating that gap filling provides independent value. The gap between h-main and h-ablation should be 0.1-0.5 points.
arms.observed: Score: 95.21 (deterministic across 2 valid runs, excluding one judge fluke at 82.51). Exactly equal to h-main. Gap filling provides zero additional value — after SA with per-item heuristic selection optimizes the packing, there are no remaining free rectangles large enough to fit any item type.
arms.diagnostic_note: Gap filling is redundant because the per-item heuristic selection in SA already achieves near-optimal space utilization. The ordered packing with individually-tuned heuristics per item type leaves no exploitable residual space. The prediction assumed sequential processing would leave gaps; in practice, per-item heuristic optimization addresses this at the heuristic-selection level rather than needing a post-hoc gap-fill pass.

discrepancy_analysis: h-main CONFIRMED (95.21 > 95.0 target, > 94.84 baseline). h-ablation REFUTED — gap filling contributes 0 points, not the predicted 0.1-0.5. The real mechanism was per-item heuristic selection via SA, not gap filling. Two SA-over-orderings-only attempts (94.84) proved the ordering space was already well-explored by hill-climbing. The joint search space (ordering × per-item heuristic) is the actual lever.
